title: 51,000 Buddhas in a Cliff, or a Temple Pinned to One? | China Travel Expert
description:
Datong, in northern Shanxi, gives you two very different ways to spend a day — and both are carved into rock.

The Yungang Grottoes are a 5th-century Buddhist cliff: UNESCO counts 252 caves and niches holding about 51,000 statues across roughly 18,000 m² of carved surface. They were cut from the middle of the 5th century into the early 6th, under the Northern Wei, and were inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2001. The earliest group, the Tanyao Five, was carved under imperial patronage.

The other option is the Hanging Temple (Xuankong Si), a monastery built onto a sheer cliff face on Mount Heng, its halls and walkways resting on beams set into the rock. Its traditional founding date of 491 comes from legend rather than a documented record, and published figures for its height above the ground vary widely — so you won't get a number for it here.

🧭 Expert Tip: at Yungang, start with the Tanyao Five — they are the earliest caves on the site.

大同两处石头上的古迹：云冈石窟，252个洞窟与壁龛、约5.1万尊造像，北魏开凿，2001年列入世界遗产；悬空寺则整座嵌在恒山崖壁上。
